economy.summary: In her Spring 2026 newsletter she says it is past time to raise Pennsylvania's minimum wage from $7.25 an hour, fully supports Gov. Shapiro's proposal to increase it to $15 by January 1, 2027, and runs a petition to raise the wage.
economy.short: Supports raising Pennsylvania's minimum wage to $15 by 2027.

taxes.summary: She says she voted for the 2025-26 state budget's Working Pennsylvanians Tax Credit, which gives households that qualify for the federal Earned Income Tax Credit an additional 10 percent savings on their state taxes.
taxes.short: Voted for state budget's tax credit for working families.

education.summary: She says she has been fighting to improve educational opportunities and highlights the 2025-26 state budget she supported for delivering school-funding increases, including 10.1 percent for the School District of Philadelphia and 22.3 percent for the William Penn School District.
education.short: Highlights supporting budget with local school-funding increases.

healthcare.summary: She says she created House Bill 654, which would help more seniors afford life-saving medications by raising the income limits for the PACENET prescription-assistance program.
healthcare.short: Sponsored bill to expand PACENET senior prescription-drug eligibility.

energy.summary: She sponsored House Bill 543, which clarifies that the Public Utility Commission cannot reject utilities' energy efficiency plans solely for including mechanical insulation, which she says is safe, standard, and improves energy efficiency.
energy.short: Sponsored bill easing energy-efficiency plans that use mechanical insulation.

guns.summary: Her public-safety work centers on combating human trafficking: she sponsored a bill requiring hotel and lodging staff to be trained to recognize and report trafficking, and she highlights a 75 percent budget increase for trafficking enforcement; her materials do not detail a firearms policy.
guns.short: Sponsored human-trafficking training bill; no firearms policy stated.
